Plainly put

What I mean by agentics

Agentic AI is software that does more than answer a question. It takes steps, uses tools, and gets work done, with people deciding what it is for and checking what it did.

So the interesting question is rarely "which tool?". It is what you hand over, who owns it, and how you know it worked.

That is what we talk about.

Three threads, one cloth

Three ways to work with me

Each of these starts the same way: a conversation.

Leadership workshop on agentics

Challenge-led. You bring a real rollout challenge and a picture of your data: what you have, where it lives, and roughly what state it is in. We work the challenge together in the room, with the people who will have to make it happen. You leave with practical rollouts you can start on, not a tour of tools.

One-to-one coaching for leaders

Time with me on how you think about agentics and how you work with it: your decisions, your organisation, the agentic work in front of you. I coach from doing it. I run my own company with agents doing much of the work, so we talk about what actually happens, not what a vendor says will happen.

Where I work

I am based in London. I work across the UK and the EU, and further afield when it makes sense.

How I work

Four years working totally with agents. Forty years in IT. One way of working that comes from both.

I run YQUP with agents doing much of the work. I check what they produce, because generating something and checking it are different jobs. That is the thread through everything I coach: people, agents and work woven together, with a person still holding the end of each thread.

I would rather show you what that means for your challenge than draw it as a diagram.

Who you work with

You work with me, Tony Wood.

Forty years in IT, and more than a decade building communities. Along the way I have been a founder, CEO, CTO, advisor and board member, across product, data, operations and governance, including in regulated environments such as banking.

Today I am:

  • Community Lead at CEO CF (the CEO Collaborative Forum)
  • Adjunct Lecturer at the University of Exeter Business School, where I teach applied technology, operational excellence, FinTech, governance and entrepreneurship
  • Leadership Fellows Programme Director at St George's House

The proof I can show you in public is the thinking and the practice. I write regularly at tonywood.org on agentic systems, governance and operations. YQUP runs the free Chief Agentic Officer Briefing. And YQUP itself runs with agents doing much of the work.

Work harnesses

Move out of chat and into the harness.

A chat can produce words. A harness lets an agentic worker see the work, use tools, change files, run checks, create reports, and bring evidence back for review.

01.

See the work

Local files, repos, documents, data, and context are available instead of pasted fragments.

02.

Use real tools

Code, scripts, browsers, checks, data tools, and plugins can be used inside the workflow.

03.

Change the artifact

The agent can update code, reports, pages, documents, and other working outputs.

04.

Verify as you go

Diffs, tests, previews, screenshots, logs, and smoke checks make quality inspectable.

05.

Keep the trail

Prompts, decisions, edits, evidence, and results become reviewable management records.

Starter harness links

Places to inspect the pattern.

The important question is not which logo wins. Ask what work it can see, what tools it can use, what it can change, how it verifies, and what evidence it leaves behind.

The Chief Agentic Officer Briefing

Get the briefing

The Chief Agentic Officer Briefing is a short UK and Europe briefing on agentic AI, written for you to scan and for your assistant to read. YQUP runs it, and it is free. No account or payment needed.

What a Chief Agentic Officer is

The person or mandate that makes agentic work owned: what exists, what it may do, who can stop it, and what leaders can inspect afterwards.

The briefing supports your judgement. It does not replace legal, regulatory, director or management judgement.

What you get

  • A plain-English read on what changed and why it may matter, across AI governance, cyber and resilience, disclosure, CSRD/ESRS, GDPR and data, and board actions.
  • Source anchors and human gates your assistant can use to brief you back, without any authority to act.
  • A short daily audio companion, on the podcast feed and Spotify.
